common_mistakes: quoted specific package prices (4000/month and 32000/year) instead of deferring to an executive.
failed to explain that the meeting is free of charge.
mispronounced 'indiamart' as 'india martins'
did not confirm the callback slot in a structured way (e.g., 'i will call you back in a week')
did not follow the 'busy' playbook by providing a one-line value proposition before asking for a callback time.
ignored seller's refusal of beauty products and mismatched profile.
failed to handle 'busy' signal by offering a callback or whatsapp alternative.
repeated the mismatch explanation multiple times without advancing the pitch.
did not use a concise value proposition before asking for time.
misinterpreted the seller's request to call back later ('baad mein baat kar loongi') as a request for a follow-up reminder instead of a direct callback.
failed to handle the seller's audio/connectivity issue ('ro nahi ro nahi aa rahi ho') with the standard 'kya aapko meri awaaz aa rahi hai?' script.
pitched pricing ('chaar hazaar ka charges') despite the playbook instructing to never quote a price.
failed to transition to the goal step after the seller expressed market slowdown interest.
quoted a specific conversion percentage (30 to 40%) and lead volume (70 leads) when the playbook strictly prohibits quoting prices or guaranteed metrics.
failed to confirm the callback slot explicitly after the seller gave a time.
misheard 'meeting' as 'mickey' when repeating the seller's statement.
continued pitching product margins (helmet) even after the seller clearly shifted to plastic frames and makhana export.
pitched product benefits ('intermart aapko customer business la ke de raha hai') instead of focusing on scheduling a meeting as per the playbook.
repeatedly pushed for a meeting even after the seller clearly stated their partner was against it and unavailable for 10-15 days.
repeatedly pitched features without confirming if the seller had any specific questions or needs first.
did not explicitly ask for the seller's preferred contact method before ending the call.
repeated the time offer twice in the same breath instead of clarifying the 'three times' confusion.
did not explicitly confirm the exact slot (5 pm or 5:30 pm) after the seller questioned the repeated connection attempts.
quoted a price: the agent did not quote a price, but it did make a confusing statement about dropping the product ('we have dropped it') which was unnecessary.
claimed to be human: the agent explicitly stated it is a virtual assistant ('indiamart se phone kar rahe ho na?').
